10pub(crate) mod scalar {
11    /// Perform an approximate division by 255.
12    ///
13    /// There are three reasons for having this method.
14    /// 1) Divisions are slower than shifting + adding, and the compiler does not seem to replace
15    ///    divisions by 255 with an equivalent (this was verified by benchmarking; doing / 255 was
16    ///    significantly slower).
17    /// 2) Integer divisions are usually not available in SIMD, so this provides a good baseline
18    ///    implementation.
19    /// 3) There are two options for performing the division: One is to perform the division
20    ///    in a way that completely preserves the rounding semantics of a integer division by
21    ///    255. This could be achieved using the implementation `(val + 1 + (val >> 8)) >> 8`.
22    ///    The second approach (used here) has slightly different rounding behavior to a
23    ///    normal division by 255, but is much faster (see <https://github.com/linebender/vello/issues/904>)
24    ///    and therefore preferable for the high-performance pipeline.
25    ///
26    /// Four properties worth mentioning:
27    /// - This actually calculates the ceiling of `val / 256`.
28    /// - Within the allowed range for `val`, rounding errors do not appear for values divisible by 255, i.e. any call `div_255(val * 255)` will always yield `val`.
29    /// - If there is a discrepancy, this division will always yield a value 1 higher than the original.
30    /// - This holds for values of `val` up to and including `65279`. You should not call this function with higher values.
31    #[inline(always)]
32    pub(crate) const fn div_255(val: u16) -> u16 {
33        debug_assert!(val < 65280, "the properties of `div_255` do not hold for values of `65280` or greater");
34        (val + 255) >> 8
35    }
36
37    #[cfg(any())]
38    mod tests {
39        use crate::third_party::vello_cpu::util::scalar::div_255;
40
41        #[cfg(any())]
42        fn div_255_properties() {
43            for i in 0_u16..256 * 255 {
44                let expected = i / 255;
45                let actual = div_255(i);
46
47                assert!(expected <= actual, "In case of a discrepancy, the division should yield a value higher than the original.");
48
49                let diff = expected.abs_diff(actual);
50                assert!(diff <= 1, "Rounding error shouldn't be higher than 1.");
51
52                if i % 255 == 0 {
53                    assert_eq!(diff, 0, "Division should be accurate for multiples of 255.");
54                }
55            }
56        }
57    }
58}

60pub(crate) trait NormalizedMulExt {
61    fn normalized_mul(self, other: Self) -> Self;
62}
63
64impl<S: Simd> NormalizedMulExt for u8x32<S> {
65    #[inline(always)]
66    fn normalized_mul(self, other: Self) -> Self {
67        let divided = (self.simd.widen_u8x32(self) * other.simd.widen_u8x32(other)).div_255();
68        self.simd.narrow_u16x32(divided)
69    }
70}

72pub(crate) trait EncodedImageExt {
73    fn has_skew(&self) -> bool;
74    fn nearest_neighbor(&self) -> bool;
75}
76
77impl EncodedImageExt for EncodedImage {
78    fn has_skew(&self) -> bool {
79        !(self.x_advance.y as f32).is_nearly_zero() || !(self.y_advance.x as f32).is_nearly_zero()
80    }
81
82    fn nearest_neighbor(&self) -> bool {
83        self.sampler.quality == ImageQuality::Low
84    }
85}

87pub(crate) trait Premultiply {
88    fn premultiply(self, alphas: Self) -> Self;
89    fn unpremultiply(self, alphas: Self) -> Self;
90}
91
92impl<S: Simd> Premultiply for f32x4<S> {
93    #[inline(always)]
94    fn premultiply(self, alphas: Self) -> Self {
95        self * alphas
96    }
97
98    #[inline(always)]
99    fn unpremultiply(self, alphas: Self) -> Self {
100        let zero = Self::splat(alphas.simd, 0.0);
101        let divided = self / alphas;
102
103        self.simd.select_f32x4(self.simd.simd_eq_f32x4(alphas, zero), zero, divided)
104    }
105}
